s.note: Wallace and his favourite crumbly cheese
s.how: Toast 8 slices of thick white bread on one side under the grill. Turn and spread the untoasted sides lightly with butter. Crumble over 200g Wensleydale mixed with 80g grated cheddar, pressing it to the edges. Grill 3 to 4 minutes until bubbling and golden in spots. Top each with a spoon of apple chutney (150g total) and a few thin slices of green apple. Cut into triangles.

s.note: Wallace's contraptions that make breakfast at the press of a button
s.how: Whisk 3 eggs with 150ml milk, 1 tbsp caster sugar and 1 tsp vanilla. Cut 6 thick slices of white bread into 3 fingers each. Dip each finger in the egg for a few seconds a side. Fry in batches in 40g butter over medium heat for 2 minutes a side until golden. Toss straight away in 50g caster sugar mixed with 1 tsp cinnamon. Serve warm with 150g strawberry jam.

m.note: a Northern English dinner at 62 West Wallaby Street
m.how: Brown 8 pork sausages slowly in a pan for 15 minutes. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and 100ml milk. Fry 2 sliced onions in the sausage pan until soft, stir in 1 tbsp flour and 400ml beef stock and simmer until thick. Serve the sausages on mash with gravy.

w.how: Rub 100g cold butter into 250g self-raising flour, add 150ml milk to make a soft dough and roll into a rectangle. Spread with 200g strawberry jam, roll up and bake on a lined tray at 190C for 35 minutes. Serve in slices with 500ml custard made from custard powder and milk.

d.note: Gromit putting his feet up at 62 West Wallaby Street
d.how: Heat 1L milk in a saucepan until steaming. Whisk in 100g chopped milk chocolate, 2 tbsp cocoa, 3 tbsp malted milk powder and 1 tbsp sugar until smooth and frothy, about 3 minutes. Do not let it boil. Whip 150ml cream to soft peaks. Pour into 4 big mugs, spoon the cream on top and grate over a little more chocolate.
